sourceNote: The Tripo P2 wolf mesh with its quads (assets/models/wolf/README.md). The hand rig assets/models/wolf/tripo-hand/wolf.blend starts from it in headless Blender with the calls of tools/blender/body_armature.py (design 4.4, "Hand rig").
name: Wolf

bind.trunkNote: The trunk of the seated bind sits upright (trunk_turn() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The pelvis turns back until the hip angle opens by open degrees, and each trunk bone takes its share. The values are those of the wolf of main (tools/mesh-rigs/wolf.json at cbc8db5e4).
bind.bindArmsNote: With straightArms, bindArms.upper_arm sets the bind upper arm, and bindArms.forearm sets only the elbow axis: the cross product of the bind upper arm and this forearm direction (Body.hinges, bind_hinges() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The two directions are those of the wolf of main (tools/mesh-rigs/wolf.json at cbc8db5e4), so that the elbow axes of the clarinet hold stay.
bind.straightArmsNote: The bind keeps the arms of the source straight: the forearm and the paw keep the turn of the upper arm, so that the rest shape holds the bend of no role, and each hold bends the elbow and the wrist from the same shape (the role-neutral bind of design 4.4).
bind.bindSupinationNote: The bind paws take no supination (paw_supination() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), so the bind forearms have no twist. The paw turn of the build sets the twist of the clarinet hold (assets/models/wolf/README.md, "Arm twist").
bind.note: legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind to the source: the thigh slopes 25 degrees down and 15 degrees out, and the shin leans 0 degrees forward of vertical, so that most of the thigh lies on the seat (uv run --no-project --with numpy python -I tools/rig/leg_turns.py <config> 25 15 0).
bind.tailBindNote: The direction of each tail bone in the seated bind (bind_turns() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), as on the wolf of main: the root goes 40 degrees below the level back over the back edge of the seat, and the tip hangs down behind the seat. In the source, the tail hangs down behind the legs.

tone.note: No move. The hand route does not read the tone. The color map of the source replaces the face colors in the app.

colors.note: Each face takes the mean sRGB color of the texture at a grid of samples. A face is dark when at least eyeShare of its samples are below dark. A dark face in the eye box is an eye, and a face in the nose box near the nose color is the nose. A palette of palette colors (k-means in Oklab) keeps the colors few.
colors.eyeBoxNote: The eye box holds the painted eye of each side (x 0.029 to 0.064, y 0.829 to 0.858, z 0.123 to 0.145 in the source). The eyes are faces of the head surface, with no eyeball. The nose box holds the dark nose (x -0.029 to 0.029, y 0.778 to 0.813, the front at z 0.241).

eyeShell.note: Each eye shell is a fan from the middle of the dark faces of the eye to at most points points of their edge, lifted along the normal of the eye. pnpm body-module drops the fan, and the app puts its pea eye there (design 4.5). The faces of the old eye take the main color of the ring around it.

chair.note: The seat is level, and its top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat, with no shin, foot, or tail (seat_masks() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The front edge lies seatGap units behind the knee joint of the bind (the property seat of the armature). The half width holds the haunch (x -0.139 to 0.139).

armSegments.note: Each upper arm and each forearm has 4 deform segments, and each elbow and wrist a helper bone of this length in units, as on the other bodies.

jointsNote: The places are the places of the source, in the body units and axes of the source pose: 1 unit from the soles to the ear tips, the soles at y = 0, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The FBX has no armature, so each joint comes from sections of the mesh and its edge loops. Arm (closed rings of 11 vertices from x 0.124 to x 0.290, axis y 0.638 to 0.627, radius 0.057 to 0.035): the shoulder joint at x 0.10, at the trunk side (x 0.099 at y 0.62), the elbow at x 0.20, at the middle from the shoulder to the wrist, the wrist at x 0.30, where the paw widens, the knuckles at x 0.355, where the digits part, the tip at x 0.409. Leg (closed rings of 11 vertices from y 0.061 to y 0.255): the hip joint at (0.067, 0.29, 0.055) in the haunch, the knee at y 0.165, between the rings at y 0.150 and 0.172, the ankle at y 0.06, the ball of the foot at z 0.09, and the toe tips at z 0.142. Trunk: the spine bones lie at about 0.35 of the depth from the back. The neck is narrowest at y 0.68 to 0.72, and the chin is at y 0.74. Ears: the root at y 0.90, the tips at (0.077, 1.0, 0.088). Tail: a loose part of the source, from its root at (0, 0.42, -0.04) back and down to its tip at (0, 0.11, -0.19). The palm is the true palm of the source: the mean normal of the paw faces that face down (x from 0.31) is (0.107, -0.994, 0.016). The paw turn of the build turns it with the paw. The edit paw of the build moves the knuckle joint and the tip of each fingers bone with the paw: the config holds the mapped places.
bodyNote: The facts of the body (BODY_FACTS of tools/body-module.ts) beside the height: the crease angle 180, so that each corner takes the mean normal of the faces at its vertex, as the smooth shading of an FBX viewer shows the source.
eyeSizeNote: The head height H of the body in units, as body-module measures it on the export, before the head size. The hand rig keeps the eyes of the mesh, so it places no pea eye.
metersPerUnitNote: The scale of the app: H (0.208109 units) is 0.369244 m, the H of the wolf of main (assets/models/wolf/wolf.rig.glb at cbc8db5e4). The fact height of the armature is the shoulder joints at this scale. The head, the trunk, the arms, and the legs keep the form of the source. The front paws are smaller than in the source (the edit paw of the build: 0.8 times as long and 0.8 times as wide past the wrist joint).
chairNote: The seat of the rig in units of this body, as the property seat of the armature of tripo-hand/wolf.blend holds it.
rollSplitNote: The simple route splits the roll segments by place (roll_split() of tools/blender/simple_rig.py). The hand rig sets the same split in the exact rows of each arm ring (assets/models/wolf/README.md, "tripo-hand/wolf.blend").
